Hi Thiago, I am Karen. I just joined the team in Houston. So, what exactly do you do?
I am a civil engineer at our office in Brazil. I work on sanitation projects for the consultancy.
Sanitation, so water and sewage? I come from transportation projects, so this is new for me.
Exactly. Our client is usually a water utility, the company that supplies water to a city.
And what does your team deliver?
My team studies the network and designs the treatment plant. My manager oversees the whole project.
Who decides in the end?
The client decides, but a lot of stakeholders give their opinion: the city, the regulator and the community.
That sounds complex. How long does a project usually take?
A study usually takes six months, and each deliverable goes to the client every month.
Perfect. Can you explain that to the whole team on Thursday? Nobody here really understands it.

Hi everyone, my name is Laura Chen, and I run the water department of a city utility in Arizona. My team supplies water to almost a million people, in one of the driest places in the country. What do I do all day? I do not design anything anymore. I oversee three engineers and a lab, and I spend most of my time with stakeholders: the city council, the farmers and the public. The hardest part of my job is not the engineering. It is explaining the engineering to people who do not care about pipes, until the day the water stops.

People always ask me what a consultant actually does, so here is my week. On Monday, my team reviews the data from the treatment plant. On Tuesday and Wednesday, I write the report, because every project has a deliverable, and the client expects it on Friday. On Thursday, I usually visit the site, which is the best part of the job. And on Friday, I present the numbers to the client. My wife says my job is simple: I tell people how much their water costs. She is not completely wrong.

First, the water utility hires the consultancy for a study. Then, the team studies the sewage network and collects the data. After that, the engineers design the treatment plant. Next, every month, a deliverable goes to the client. Finally, the stakeholders give their opinion and the client decides.
